| rf_ask_plain | The site's instructions file for automated visitors (robots.txt), which search engines also request as a matter of course. |
| rf_fail | Either the host serves no robots.txt, which under the robots.txt standard actually permits every crawler, or its robots.txt tells at least one of the listed crawler tokens not to fetch the path. Neither is a claim that crawlers cannot reach the data: robots.txt is a stated policy, not a barrier, and telling a training-only crawler not to fetch does not keep a page out of answer engines. |
| rf_fix_line | Serve a robots.txt that permits the data paths for the crawlers you want to allow. |
| rf_hypothesis | Does the host's declared crawler policy let SI systems' crawlers fetch the data page? Answer engines that ground on the live web honor robots.txt; a page their crawler is told not to fetch is not read by that engine. |
| rf_name_brief | Whether the site's visitor rules let AI tools in |
| rf_not_measured | The public client could not read the robots.txt, for one of three reasons: the host refused the identified client (three of sixteen hosts on the cycle of record); the client's own compliance with the site's robots.txt kept it from the file; or it could not confirm the file's state because of a server or network error. |
| rf_partial | For some of the agency's data pages the stated policy allowed all eight listed crawler tokens and for some it did not. |
| rf_pass | The host's robots.txt, as stated, allows each of eight listed crawler tokens to fetch the data page's path. Every data page that was looked at met this. |
| rf_plain_name | robots.txt permits eight listed crawler tokens |
| rf_question | Does the host's stated policy in its robots.txt allow the crawlers that answer engines use to fetch the data page? |
